So what’s up? Ryan Murphy has hardly become ratings poison, of course. And despite his outsize profile (more on that below), Murphy’s brand of provocative and often R-rated mayhem and smack-talking has always been hit-and-miss with general audiences. I asked Nielsen for total viewership numbers for

In fact, as my colleague Julia Alexander noted yesterday, Disney+/Hulu still leans more than any other streamer on old, library series with hundreds of episodes, like Grey’s Anatomy and Family Guy, as well as the kids’ stuff like Bluey. The newer offerings? Not so much. Despite a regular slate of or

Which Brings Us Back to Murphy… Despite the cuts to its overall content output, Disney has continued to invest freely in the Murphy conveyor belt of shows, even renewing All’s Fair for a second season despite U.S. numbers on par with The Beauty, which was canceled. (Maybe Kardashian’s Hulu reality s

Dana Walden needs new TV hits, and happily welcomed the star showrunner back after his Netflix run. But while Murphy’s generated no shortage of buzz (Love Story, All’s Fair, and his latest, The Shards), it translates less often to Nielsen magic.

XGIMI Titan Noir Max Specs The XGIMI Titan Noir Max is clearly built as a no-compromise, high-end RGB laser DLP projector, combining next-gen hardware with a strong focus on contrast, brightness, and installation flexibility. At its core, the projector uses a 0.47-inch SST DMD from Texas Instruments

The Lens, a High-End State of the Art This is where things get really interesting… because XGIMI didn’t just throw a decent lens on the Titan Noir Max and call it a day. They actually went all in. The projector uses the X-Master Red Ring Lens Pro, an improved version of the already excellent lens we

I honestly do not understand why XGIMI chose this rather inconvenient navigation system for the Titan Noir Max menus, because there does not seem to be any real benefit to it, and it simply makes it harder for the user to read and select what they want.

I precisely measured these laser pulses on the Titan Noir Max using an oscilloscope, and in order to better understand the performance of XGIMI’s RBE Reduction system, I directly compared it with the corresponding implementation from AWOL Vision on the Aetherion MAX.

This is the measurement that captures the laser pulses of the Titan Noir Max in Standard Picture Mode, with the Standard White Balance selected. The RBE Reduction function is disabled. On the right, you can also see how these laser pulses appear on the screen, captured directly with my camera.

The shape of the pulses, the number of pulses, their intensity, and even the duty cycle naturally change depending on the brightness level and the color content of the frame being displayed. For example, the measurements you are looking at here were taken while the projector was displaying a 100 IRE

But how can we evaluate whether an RBE Reduction system works well, and determine how refined it really is? There are several ways to do this, but I chose the most scientific one: measuring two projectors equipped with RBE Reduction systems using an oscilloscope, and then directly comparing those me

As for the dynamic iris, personally, I was not particularly impressed. In its attempt to avoid the typical “pumping” effect, where the iris constantly opens and closes during scene transitions and becomes distracting, and honestly, XGIMI was right to avoid that, the company made the dynamic iris beh

Actually, I would go even further and place it right behind the latest JVC D-ILA projectors across all projector categories in terms of contrast performance, and honestly, I think that says everything. HDR – Dolby Vision

The tuning that Harman Kardon has done on this sound system is sick. Totally sick. The Titan Noir Max features a complete built-in audio system consisting of two full-range drivers rated at 2x12W.
